newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten presses for UK passports for HK minorities.
newsitem.headline: Patten presses for UK passports for HK minorities.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday that pressing Britain to grant passports to ethnic minorities facing statelessness in the territory after its handover to China remained one of his main tasks.

The Hong Kong government has estimated that approximately 8,000 members of Hong Kong's minorities, of mainly Indian and Pakistani descent, face statelessness when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
At present they are entitled to a British Overseas passport which gives them the right to travel but not to full British citizenship and the right to live and work in the United Kingdom.

"I am fully convinced that the United Kingdom ought to grant full British citizenship to those members of the non-Chinese ethnic minorities...possessing no other nationality," Patten told an Indian Association lunch.
He said there was support for his views in both houses of the British parliament.
"There is great support for this cause. It will not diminish. Nor will my determination to June 1997," Patten said. "That remains one of my main tasks in the coming weeks and months."
